lore: Every crate of figures that leaves the counting house is sealed in wax with the census it was counted from. Customs Officer Perpetua breaks no seals: she recounts the cargo herself against tonight's census and the harbour's current rules, and only then presses her stamp. A crate counted from an old census, a crate whose seal is missing, and a crate whose numbers were changed after sealing all stay on the quay.

lines.sealed: Recounted and true. My stamp is on it; let it sail.
lines.stale: This was counted from an old census or under old rules. Count it again.
lines.tampered: Same census, different numbers. Someone wrote on this after the wax set.
lines.unsealed: No seal, no census named. I cannot tell where these figures came from.
